jaegertracing/jaeger#9789.title: ClickHouse spans table omits schema_url, flags and dropped counts from the OTLP span
jaegertracing/jaeger#9789.body:
## Problem

The ClickHouse `spans` table (`internal/storage/v2/clickhouse/sql/create_spans_table.sql`) stores nearly every OTLP span field, but the writer (`dbmodel/to.go`) and reader (`dbmodel/from.go`) have no column for these, so a span written to ClickHouse and read back loses them:

| OTLP field | Level |
|---|---|
| `schema_url` | resource |
| `schema_url` | scope |
| `flags` | span |
| `dropped_attributes_count` | span, event, link, scope |
| `dropped_events_count` | span |
| `dropped_links_count` | span |
| `flags` | link |

The two `schema_url` fields matter beyond fidelity: RFC 0005 lists `resource.schemaURL` and `scope.schemaURL` as built-in filter fields, and ClickHouse is the only backend that declares all five levels, so these are the only two RFC 0005 built-in fields whose absence is a schema gap rather than unfinished lowering (#9701 maps five fields and can add the rest from existing columns).

The dropped counts and flags carry no filter use, but a round trip through storage should not silently zero them, and the v1 storage integration suite does not notice because its fixtures leave them at zero.

## Proposal

Add the missing columns to the spans table and wire them through `SpanRow`, `ToDBModel` and `FromDBModel`:

- `resource_schema_url String`, `scope_schema_url String`
- `flags UInt32`, `dropped_attributes_count UInt32`, `dropped_events_count UInt32`, `dropped_links_count UInt32`
- `events.dropped_attributes_count`, `links.dropped_attributes_count`, `links.flags`, `scope_dropped_attributes_count`

A corpus fixture with non-zero values for each field makes the round trip a shared integration assertion rather than a ClickHouse-only test.

## Schema migration

This is the first change to the ClickHouse schema after it reached users, so it has to establish how the schema is amended. Today `newSchemaBuilder` (`internal/storage/v2/clickhouse/factory.go`) runs one set of `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` statements at startup; against an existing deployment those are no-ops, so the new columns would never appear and the writer would fail on the first insert.

The mechanism should be forward-only numbered migrations that the binary applies itself at startup, with a table recording which ones have run, as Flyway and golang-migrate do, rather than operator-run scripts in the style of the Cassandra `migration/` directory. Adopt [golang-migrate](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate) for it:

- Import only `migrate/v4`, `database/clickhouse` and `source/iofs`. Drivers are opt-in by import path, so the build compiles seven packages from the module and no third-party module beyond it; the other databases' drivers stay out of the build and of `go.sum`.
- Migration files live in an `embed.FS` beside the current SQL, named `000001_initial_schema.up.sql`, `000002_otlp_span_fields.up.sql`, and so on. Forward-only: no `down` files, since dropping a column that has received data is never something the binary should do on its own.
- The driver connects through `database/sql`; `clickhouse.OpenDB` from clickhouse-go v2 produces that handle from the same options the factory already parses, and `WithInstance` takes it.
- Behind the existing `create_schema` flag: when it is on, the binary runs `Up()` and applies pending steps; when it is off, the operator applies the same files by hand and the binary only checks the recorded version and refuses to start if it is newer than the one it ships with. No new configuration.
- Each step is limited to metadata-only changes (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, which does not rewrite MergeTree parts) and to dropping and recreating materialized views. A change that would rewrite a table is not a startup migration and stops with instructions for the operator.

Two settings to decide when the first migration lands:

- The version table `schema_migrations` defaults to the `TinyLog` engine, which is right for a single node; a replicated deployment needs a `MergeTree` family engine, and the driver's `ClusterName` option adds `ON CLUSTER` to its own statements.
- A file with several statements needs the driver's multi-statement mode (`x-multi-statement`), which splits on `;` with a size cap.

## Concurrent instances

golang-migrate's ClickHouse driver gives idempotence, not mutual exclusion. Its `Lock()` is a process-local atomic flag, so it serializes `Up()` calls inside one process only; the Postgres and MySQL drivers take a database lock (`pg_advisory_lock`, `GET_LOCK`), but ClickHouse has no advisory locks and the driver does not emulate one. Two Jaeger instances starting against the same database can therefore both read version 1 and both run step 2. What follows:

- `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent and ClickHouse serializes `ALTER`s on a table, so the schema is correct whoever finishes second.
- `schema_migrations` is append-only with a `sequence` column and `Version()` reads the newest row, so two instances recording version 2 leave a harmless duplicate.
- An instance that reads the version while another has written its "version 2, dirty" row fails to start with `ErrDirty`. That is one replica failing startup, not corruption, and it clears on its next restart.
- A non-idempotent step, such as dropping and recreating a materialized view, is where a race could lose data, and that step is unsafe even single-process because inserts during the gap bypass the view.

Jaeger closes the gap with two measures:

1. **Every step is idempotent and re-runnable.** Columns are added with `IF NOT EXISTS`, views are created with `IF NOT EXISTS` or changed with `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY QUERY` rather than dropped and recreated, and the smoke test applies each migration twice and requires the second run to be a no-op.
2. **A dirty or locked version at startup means another instance is migrating.** The binary re-reads the version with backoff for a bounded time before failing, instead of failing on the first `ErrDirty`. For large fleets the docum

jaegertracing/jaeger#9631.title: [Feature]: Support pagination in query APIs
jaegertracing/jaeger#9631.body:
## Requirement

A client of the trace search API must be able to retrieve every matching trace, not only the first page. Today `FindTraces` and `FindTraceSummaries` return one page capped by `search_depth`, and everything past the cap is unreachable. The UI cannot offer "load more", and a program walking a time window cannot know whether it saw the whole result.

## Design

[RFC 0014](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/main/docs/rfc/0014-search-result-pagination.md) settles how this is done: an opaque `page_token` the caller echoes back for the next page, a `next_page_token` on the response, and a `paginated` capability that a backend declares so that one which cannot paginate serves a single capped page and says so, rather than returning a wrong one. Offset paging (`limit`/`offset` as in the v1 API) was weighed there and rejected (§3, §10), so a PR adding an `offset` parameter will be closed.

## Status

Delivered:
- M1 protos, in https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-idl/pull/213.
- M2 storage contract, query-service admission and the `PageChunk` response envelope, in #9570, #9450 and #9585.

Open, in order:
- The `paginated` entry in the capabilities the UI reads, and the §3.2 token fingerprint once a backend mints tokens.
- M3 Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, the first paginating backend.
- M4 remote-storage gRPC.
- M5 UI "load more".

Each milestone in the RFC has an exit bar. Pick one, say so here before starting, and keep one milestone per PR.

Supersedes #9369 and #2027, which asked for this with the v1 `offset` model.

comments.author: alishair7071
comments.body:
@yurishkuro after checking the options, I don’t see a query-only way to keep both exact trace pagination and the current newest-first ordering on the existing span documents.

Elasticsearch/OpenSearch require `collapse` and `search_after` to sort by the same field. So collapsing on `traceID` can page traces, but it cannot also sort by `(max(startTime), traceID)`. Composite aggregation can page trace-ID buckets, but it likewise cannot order those buckets by the `max(startTime)` metric.

I see two viable directions:

1. Preserve newest-first ordering by introducing a trace-level search representation with the ordering key stored per trace, then paginate that representation by `(startTime, traceID)`. This is a larger change involving indexing and likely backfill.
2. Keep the existing span index and use collapse plus `search_after` on `traceID` alone. That is supported, but changes the result ordering and would require an explicit change to the RFC’s ordering requirement.

I don’t think either trade-off should be chosen implicitly. Which requirement would you prefer to prioritize for M3? I am happy to help investigate or prototype the agreed direction.

grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway#7281.title: Insecure default header matcher
grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway#7281.body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

We recently had a very serious CVE in our project https://docs.velociraptor.app/announcements/advisories/cve-2026-18972/ due to the default header matcher in grpc gateway. 

The default header matcher copies all HTTP headers into the grpc metadata without filtering, allowing arbitrary metadata items to be added unexpectedly. If the user of grpc gateway does not set a specific header matcher with runtime.WithIncomingHeaderMatcher() option this can pollute the metadata with unexpected values injected by the http header.

I think a better more secure design is a noop header matcher which requires deliberately accepting some headers to be forwarded to the metadata.  (i.e. opt in rather than opt out). If the user is trying to capture specific headers then they should declare those specific headers to be injected into the grpc metadata.

## To Reproduce

The default runtime.NewServeMux( ) installs a default header matcher which copies all headers to the grpc metadata.

## Expected behavior

If a new user does not carefully review all documentation they would expect the grpc metadata to be clean and free for spurious values.

## Actual Behavior

In the default configuration, grpc metadata items can be injected by external HTTP headers.

## Your Environment

All supported Go versions and OSs.

comments.author: johanbrandhorst

We've just [started working](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7282) on a Security Considerations section of our docs, this sounds like something that belongs on there. Do you think there is anything else we can do to help others avoid this issue? I am not convinced this behaviour is in itself a security issue. Changing the behavior would risk breaking existing users, obviously.

comments.author: scudette
johanbrandhorst
comments.body: Thanks for your thoughtful reply. I don't know how many of our users rely on the automatic HTTP header conversion, but I'm tempted to agree that we should change it, at least the `MetadataHeaderPrefix` stripping logic. We could introduce a new `WithLegacyHeaderMatching` option to restore the old behavior. Would you be interested in helping contribute a fix for this?

comments.author: scudette
comments.body:
Happy to prepare a PR. I propose the following changes

1. The default header matcher should be a noop header matcher which does not propagate anything.
2. The WithLegacyHeaderMatching will install the current default with the current behavior.

If users need to pass a specific header they will need to install a custom header matchers (like the example above). This might also require a documentation change.

This change is not backwards compatible and will result in a breakage upon upgrade for people who currently rely on the current behavior - but this is good IMHO because if they are relying on it , further review might determine they are susceptible to an auth bypass vulnerability.

Currently, when writing out any annotation streams, the label information (e.g. P, S, D) is often lost as obspy performs an internal conversion to a C struct where the **trace.stats.channel** parameter cannot be be greater than 11 bytes. ends up with **zero fault references on its builder**. The implicit foliation
field is built smoothly across every fault and extracted isosurfaces are
continuous meshes that show no fault offset — even though the fault features
themselves are interpolated and exist in the model.

The data needed to construct the proper mapping is already in the `.loop3d`
(`eventRelationships` carries the unit-fault crossings that map2loop's
Stage 4 topology produces). It is simply never read.

The result: the same map2loop output produces **two different LoopStructural
models** depending on which processor consumes it. `Map2LoopProcessor`
builds `fault_stratigraphy` correctly from its `fault_strat` DataFrame;
`LoopProjectfileProcessor` discards the relationships. The `.loop3d` is
supposed to be a faithful re-encoding, and today it is lossy for the
unit-fault mapping.

## Versions affected

| | Version | `fault_stratigraphy=None` hardcoded |
|---|---|---|
| LoopStructural released | 1.6.27 | ✓ |
| LoopStructural released | 1.6.28 | ✓ |
| LoopStructural `master` HEAD | (current) | ✓ |

Confirmed on Python 3.12, conda-forge / loop3d channels. `LoopProjectFile`
0.2.2, `map2loop` 3.3.1.

## Reproduction

```python
from LoopProjectFile import ProjectFile
from LoopStructural.modelling.input.project_file import LoopProjectfileProcessor
from LoopStructural import GeologicalModel

# Any .loop3d with stratigraphy + faults works. E.g. the bundled map2loop
# Hamersley demo (Project(use_australian_state_data="WA", ...).run_all()).
pf = ProjectFile("hamersley.loop3d")
proc = LoopProjectfileProcessor(pf)

assert proc.fault_stratigraphy is None  # the bug — should be a dict

model = GeologicalModel.from_processor(proc)
model.update()

sg = model['sg']
print(len(sg.faults))  # 0 — should be N
```

The foliation has zero fault references even though the model knows
about every fault.

## Empirical evidence

Sampling the foliation scalar field on a horizontal slice of the bundled
Hamersley demo, both with the existing `None` and with
`_fault_stratigraphy = {sg: [all_fault_names]}` set on the processor:

```
Configuration                           | mean |Δfield| | nonzero diff cells
----------------------------------------+--------------+-------------------
fault_stratigraphy=None  (current)      |   reference  |   reference
fault_stratigraphy populated, 1× disp   |        0.00  |   0 / 15717
fault_stratigraphy populated, 50× disp  |     2248.91  |  15717 / 15717
```

The 1× test is identical to within float precision — not because the fix
is a no-op, but because map2loop emits a placeholder `100 m` displacement
when the source has no throw measurements, and 100 m is invisible against
the Hamersley regional ~6 km vertical signal. The 50× test (5000 m,
geologically realistic) produces visibly chopped layers and a synclinal
warp — proving the wiring works end-to-end.

## Asymmetry between processors

| | `Map2LoopProcessor` | `LoopProjectfileProcessor` |
|---|---|---|
| Source | map2loop output dir | `.loop3d` (re-encoded map2loop output) |
| Builds `fault_stratigraphy` | ✓ from `fault_strat` DataFrame | ✗ hardcodes `None` |
| Stratigraphy gets fault refs | ✓ | ✗ |
| Visible fault offset in surfaces | ✓ | ✗ |

## Root cause

`LoopStructural/modelling/input/project_file.py`, in
`LoopProjectfileProcessor.__init__`:

```python
        super().__init__(
            ...
            fault_properties=fault_properties,
            fault_edges=fault_edges,
            colours=colours,
            fault_stratigraphy=None,      # ← here
            intrusions=None,
            ...
        )
```

Secondary: `fault_stratigraphy` is exposed on `ProcessInputData`
as a property **without a setter**, so users who notice cannot set it
post-construction through the public API — they must write to
`_fault_stratigraphy` directly.

## Proposed fix

Two-tier, with a small extra:

**Tier 1 — read the relationships from the `.loop3d`.**
The data is in `pf.eventRelationships` (or the equivalent eventLinks /
faultLog tables Stage 4 topology populates). Build the mapping the same
shape `Map2LoopProcessor` produces:

```python
# Sketch — exact column names depend on the .loop3d schema
fault_stratigraphy = {sg: [] for sg in stratigraphic_supergroups}
for row in pf.eventRelationships.itertuples():
    fname = self._fault_id_to_name.get(row.eventId1)
    uname = self._strat_id_to_name.get(row.eventId2)
    if fname and uname:
        fault_stratigraphy[supergroup_for(uname)].append(fname)
fault_stratigraphy = {sg: sorted(set(f)) for sg, f in fault_stratigraphy.items() if f}
```

**Tier 2 — fallback.** When `eventRelationships` is empty/missing,
default to "every fault cuts every supergroup":

```python
if not fault_stratigraphy:
    fault_stratigraphy = {sg: list(fault_names) for sg in stratigraphic_supergroups}
```

Strictly better than `None`, and matches the standard assumption in
LoopStructural tutorials when users don't supply per-unit relationships.

**Tier 3.** Add a setter to the `fault_stratigraphy` property on
`ProcessInputData` so consumers can set it post-construction.

## Workaround until the fix lands

```python
processor = LoopProjectfileProcessor(pf)
processor._fault_stratigraphy = {  # write to backing field; property has no setter
    sg: list(processor.fault_network.faults)
    for sg in processor.stratigraphic_column.keys()
    if sg != "faults"
}
model = GeologicalModel.from_processor(processor)
model.update()
```

Applies Tier 2 only (every fault cuts every supergroup). Produces correct
fault wiring; visible offset still depends on having realistic displacement
values in the source data — map2loop's de

napari/napari#789.body:
## 🚀 Feature

We've been chatting with the FlyEM folks at Janelia about putting their data in napari, whether it would scale, the various ways to interact with it, etc. As a first step, it would be great to build a proof of concept accessing a DVID volume as a dask array. @DocSavage shared the following DVID endpoint URLs with me as a first pass, with the caveat that they might move in ~2-3 months. But it should be enough to get us started.

-------------------------------
 
Here are the relevant endpoints to access DVID directly:
 
MUSHROOM BODY dataset – grayscale only
https://emdata.janelia.org/api/repo/ee789/info
This will give you JSON describing the metadata for the Mushroom body dataset, which is 7615 x 11139 x 14655 voxels.  So it’s a reasonable size.
 
For the grayscale (uint8blk) you can access documentation for the HTTP API here:
https://emdata.janelia.org/api/node/ee789/grayscale/help
If you scroll down to the /raw or /blocks endpoint, that will let you download the raw data.
 
There’s a JPEG (3D) compression version with multiscale under the names grayscalejpeg, grayscalejpeg_1, … grayscalejpeg_7.

7 medulla column (version 82252).
If you do http://emdata.janelia.org/api/repo/82252/info you will see the metadata for it.
It’s a bit smaller at about 5k x 4.5k x 8k.  The grayscale is called grayscaleview, grayscaleview_1, etc.
 
Segmentation is available under the name “groundtruth”.
You can see the REST API for that type of data here:
https://emdata.janelia.org/api/node/82252/groundtruth/help
 
Like above, you can use /raw or /blocks endpoints to grab the data.
Pseudocolored segmentation:
https://emdata.janelia.org/api/node/82252/groundtruth/pseudocolor/xy/512_512/2500_2600_4000
The matching grayscale at high-res:
https://emdata.janelia.org/api/node/82252/grayscaleview/raw/xy/512_512/2500_2600_4000

-------------------------------

The first step would be to read those docs, use `da.from_delayed` to build an array from DVID endpoints, and then produce a usage example in the `examples/` folder that reads in that data.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

admin/ui

### Describe the bug

If you remove roles from a user Keycloak since 26.6.x uses a bulk operation and resource path `ui-ext/role-mapping-delete/users/<userid>` as admin event. While this is shown under the general Admin Events of the realm, it is not visible in the Admin Events of the corresponding user.
Operations that add a role to a user on the other hand are shown there.

### Version

26.8.1

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The role removal event is shown for each user in its related admin events as well

### Actual behavior

It is not shown.

### How to Reproduce?

- Enable admin events
- Create a user
- Assign him some roles -> check admin events of the user -> visible (correct)
- Remove the roles -> check admin events of the user -> not visible (only in the general admin events of the realm)

### Anything else?

It is a bit odd that adding roles to a user is handled as separate events (one event per role), while (since 26.6) the removal of multiple roles is just a single event. That is not consistent, that is why I can't propose whether this is a sole ui fix or if it is just wrong doing it in a bulk way.

testcontainers/testcontainers-java#1406.title: Image cache lookup should support SHA256 digests and Image IDs
testcontainers/testcontainers-java#1406.body:
See #1391 (and this _may_ be related to #699):

Testcontainers' image indexing code can't handle images that have SHA256 digests. We need a way to access the RepoDigests from docker-java's Image class. Unless I'm missing something, at the moment only RepoTags is mapped.

We would then modify `RemoteDockerImage`:
```
                List<Image> updatedImages = listImagesCmd.exec();
                updatedImages.stream()
                    .map(Image::getRepoTags)
                    .filter(Objects::nonNull)
                    .flatMap(Stream::of)
                    .map(DockerImageName::new)
                    .collect(Collectors.toCollection(() -> AVAILABLE_IMAGE_NAME_CACHE));
```

so that both `Image::getRepoTags` and `Image::getRepoDigests` are loaded into the cache. There's probably also some work to do around identity/equals/hashcode of `DockerImageName` objects in the cache.

EDIT 5 June 2020: We should also ensure that Image IDs are loaded into the cache - see #699.
